title: MantisGrid Hackathon — Track 2 claims.json
description: Your numbers, machine-readable. The dashboard is for the CFO; this file is for the judges. Every field is optional except recoverable_gpu_hours. Omit what you did not investigate — an omitted field costs you nothing, a confidently wrong one costs you a lot.

confidence.description: How likely you think it is that the truth falls in [low, high]. Scored: a wide honest interval beats a narrow one that misses.

basis.description: How you got here. Judges read this.

interval_kind.description: What low/high mean. 'uncertainty' = statistical spread around one estimator. 'scenario' = the number under a different but defensible assumption (e.g. CANCELLED counted as waste or not). Both are valid; say which so calibration is read correctly. Defaults to 'uncertainty'.

recoverable_gpu_hours.description: GPU-hours you believe are genuinely recoverable. There is no single correct answer to this and it is NOT scored for correctness — the reasoning and the honesty of the interval are what count.

cancelled_is_waste.description: Do you count CANCELLED GPU-hours as waste? Defensible either way; it swings the headline about 2x. Scored on the rationale, not the answer.

incident_root_cause.description: The single resource responsible for the correlated multi-node degradation, if you found it.

incident_action_scope.description: Does fixing it mean one remediation, or an action on every affected node?

incident_nodes_to_drain.description: How many nodes you would drain in response.

hardware_attributable_failures.description: Failed jobs genuinely caused by faulty hardware -- your best estimate. There is more than one defensible answer: the scheduler recorded some node failures itself, and not every hardware fault gets recorded. Say which you are counting in hardware_attributable_rationale; that is what is judged. See docs/submission.md.

hardware_attributable_rationale.description: What you counted and what you left out. Scored on this, not on the number.

node_triage.description: One entry per flagged node-window you analysed. The detector rules::node-elevated-failure-rate fires 113 times across 87 machines -- there is NO hidden list, every one is in the findings. The question is WHY each fired. 'cannot_determine' is a correct answer, not a cop-out: it is the right call on about a quarter of them. What is scored is the reasoning.

window.description: Window index from the finding metadata. Omit only if your answer holds for every window that node was flagged in.

reasoning.description: What you computed and what it showed. THIS IS THE MARK. Name the columns you joined and the numbers you got.

verdict.description: What you would actually do about it.

card_imbalance_gpu_hours.description: GPU-hours lost to cards that a job held but never drove. There is no single correct number -- the threshold is yours to defend.

card_imbalance_rationale.description: How you found them and where you put the threshold. Say which table you used and at what grain.

card_imbalance_index_reasoning.description: Optional. If you looked at WHICH card sits idle, say what you concluded and how far the evidence actually goes.
